Our goal is to create a smart insole for diabetic patients living with type 2 diabetes. record.what_it_is: Web app that finds a meeting spot for a friend group by computing an inverse-weighted midpoint of everyone's locations, then searching Google Maps for places near it.
record.problem_and_user: Friend groups scattered across Dallas-Fort Worth who struggle to pick a fair meeting place without someone driving much farther.
record.one_line_pitch: Finds a fair meeting spot for a friend group by computing an inverse-weighted midpoint of everyone's location and searching nearby places.
record.target_user: Friend groups in the same metro area
record.problem_statement: Friends scattered across a metro area struggle to pick a meeting place without one person driving far.
record.devpost_tagline: A better way to hangout with friends!
devpost_first_sections: Our friend group lives scattered across DFW, so it can be very time-consuming to decide on a place to meet where the drive isn't too out of the way for one person. This led to us coming up with the idea of WTM. A survey by Eventbrite revealed that 69% of individuals find it difficult to coordinate plans with friends due to varying schedules and locations. We want to ensure that meeting spots can be conveniently decided on without the hassle of checking the distance from everyone.

WTM calculates a user's inverse weighted midpoint between them and their friends and then uses that coordinate to find a point of interest of choice near the midpoint. This ensures everyone has a proportional drive to stay efficient on gas and time.

Roam reads it for you.

Roam is a Chrome extension that runs silently while you scroll Instagram and TikTok. It detects travel content, measures your genuine engagement with each destination, and builds an Intent Score — a quantified measure of subconscious travel desire. No forms. No chatbots. The confusion caused by completely different stories emerging from various media outlets intrigued us. We felt inspired to use our skills in web dev, AI, and a passion for data visualization to try and bring some clarity.

Our solution is a dynamic dashboard presenting how the situation unfolded up to the present, thanks to near real-time data updating based on the latest news, from both regime-controlled and independent media outlets. On our Grafana dashboard, you can: See a semi-live map pinpointing reported protest locations across Serbia. Explore sentiment analysis: How are students or protesters being portrayed? Compare keyword usage: How often do protest related terms like "justice" appear in different media spheres in comparison to pure propaganda? record.devpost_tagline: Lucid Voice gives people who can't speak their voice back: a few taps become a full sentence in their own voice, shaped to who they're talking to, and fully private on-device.
devpost_first_sections: An estimated five million Americans and nearly a hundred million people worldwide cannot rely on their own voice, from ALS, stroke, autism, or cerebral palsy. The cruelest part of conditions like aphasia is that the person knows exactly what they want to say but cannot get the words out , and today's tools are slow and robotic. We wanted to build something that knows the person and gives them their own voice back .

Lucid Voice turns two or three tapped words into a full, natural sentence, spoken in a clone of the person's own voice . It is not autocomplete : it understands who they are talking to, so the same words become "sweetie" for a daughter and "mijo" for a grandson, and it learns their style the more they use it. Behind it is a personal "brain," a living model of their world that you can watch think, learn, and grow , and the whole thing runs on-device and offline so their private words never leave their hands.

record.what_it_is: A finance dashboard with a Mapbox 3D globe that shows how news events spread as market shocks across countries, sectors and S&P 100 stocks, with LSTM price forecasts, a RAG analyst chat and a what-if event simulator.
record.problem_and_user: Headlines about outages, export limits and strikes are read in isolation although they move markets; aimed at learners and, later, institutional desks lacking expensive terminals.
record.one_line_pitch: Platform mapping how global news events ripple as financial shocks across countries, sectors and S&P 100 stocks, with a 3D globe, forecasts and what-if simulation.
record.problem_statement: Connecting geopolitical and supply-chain events to market impact normally requires costly institutional terminals unavailable to ordinary people.
record.devpost_tagline: An intelligence platform that predicts market shocks from news events.
devpost_first_sections: A semiconductor plant fire in Taiwan. An export restriction in Brussels. A port strike in Long Beach. Individually, they're headlines. Together, they're market forces — but connecting the dots across geographies, sectors, and supply chains is something only institutional desks with billion-dollar terminals can do. A 2025 systematic review of 37 papers found that "interactive methods for teaching risk and reward remain limited" and "tools rarely integrate multiple content areas, limiting their ability to convey real-world financial complexity." Nexus is an intelligence platform that maps how global events propagate as financial shockwaves across countries, sectors, and stocks. It continuously ingests news, classifies events with our own NLP models, and scores every tracked stock using a composite shock formula combining semantic similarity, historical sensitivity, geographic proximity, and supply chain linkage. glance.what: Expungement service for clearing criminal records, per the tagline; cover is a Cal Hacks logo.
glance.why: Makes clearing old records accessible to people with records.

record.what_it_is: A web app that reads an uploaded court or RAP sheet, checks the person's expungement eligibility against state law, suggests next steps if not eligible, auto-fills forms if eligible, and offers a live voice agent for guidance.
record.problem_and_user: People with past convictions who find the expungement process hard to navigate; legal aid groups named as future partners.
record.one_line_pitch: Web platform that reads uploaded court or RAP sheets, judges criminal record expungement eligibility against state law, talks users through it by voice and fills forms.
record.problem_statement: Expungement information is hard to find and the official process is long and confusing for people with old convictions.
record.devpost_tagline: Making expungement simple and accessible for all.
devpost_first_sections: Our inspiration behind our idea was to make expungement (the process of dismissing an old conviction) easier for people to access. It can be incredibly hard to find information, know what you need, and successfully go through the long official process. Our website asks the user a few simple questions and looks at their court documents to determine if they are eligible for expungement. If they aren't, it suggests next steps for the user to become eligible. If they are, it fills out the forms for them, simple as that.

Expungo is an AI-powered platform that simplifies and automates the criminal record expungement process by analyzing uploaded documents to determine eligibility. Users simply upload their court or RAP sheet and review their case directly with Expungo’s live voice agent for personalized, step-by-step guidance. All data is processed entirely in memory — ensuring that sensitive user information remains secure and confidential.

glance.what: AI Toyota recommender that asks what you want and suggests matching models.
glance.why: Matches buyers to the right Toyota without endless browsing.

record.what_it_is: A React site where the user picks a vehicle type and sets budget, credit score and down payment sliders; Claude 3.5 Sonnet with a web-search tool returns 4-6 current Toyota matches with estimated payments and pros and cons.
record.problem_and_user: Toyota shoppers who want quick recommendations with monthly financing or lease estimates instead of long research.
record.one_line_pitch: Toyota shopping assistant: pick vehicle type, budget, credit score and down payment, and Claude with web search returns four to six matching models with payments.
record.problem_statement: Researching Toyotas and real financing or lease payments takes far too long.
record.devpost_tagline: An AI Powered Toyota Car Recommendation
devpost_first_sections: What if an AI could just ask you a few questions and instantly hand you the perfect Toyota with real monthly payments?” That spark turned into Buyota – an AI-powered Toyota shopping assistant that feels like chatting with the world’s smartest car expert.

Buyota is a web app that turns 30 minutes of research into 30 seconds of magic. Pick your vehicle type (Sedan, SUV, Truck, Hybrid, Any) Slide your budget, credit score, and down payment Hit “Find My Toyota!” Claude 3.5 Sonnet instantly searches the web, pulls the latest 2024–2025 Toyota models, calculates real financing & lease payments based on your credit score, and returns 4–6 perfect matches with pros/cons and direct Toyota.com links. No more guessing games – just your dream Toyota, priced for your wallet.

glance.what: Side-by-side Toyota vs rival comparison using government data and LLM arguments.
glance.why: Shows buyers facts that favor Toyota, backed by data.

record.what_it_is: A solo Python script that compares Toyota vehicles with competitors using public safety and government data, then asks an LLM to write a verbal argument for Toyota from the inputs.

record.devpost_tagline: Toyota vehicles are superior to the competition, but this isn't always made clear to the customers. I can collect data from reliable Government sources and a LLM can make a verbal argument.

Compares Toyota vehicles to competition and highlights Toyota's strengths with real-world data scraped from reliable sources (mostly government). Since everything has to have genAI in it, I added an LLM API call to generate a verbal argument from the input parameters.

glance.what: AI wardrobe assistant tracking worn clothes and nudging you to wear more of your closet.
glance.why: Saves money by making you wear what you already own, against waste.

record.what_it_is: Streamlit wardrobe assistant that classifies clothing from photos using vision LLMs, tracks what you wear, emails you about items left unworn, and can list unwanted pieces for sale.
record.problem_and_user: Shoppers who spend heavily on clothes but wear little of them, creating waste.
record.one_line_pitch: Wardrobe manager that classifies clothing from photos with vision LLMs, tracks wear patterns, emails reminders about unworn items and helps list them for sale.
record.target_user: fashion-conscious consumers wanting to reduce clothing waste
record.problem_statement: People buy lots of clothing but wear little of it, creating waste and fashion landfill.
record.devpost_tagline: Vestique, your AI wardrobe assistant, tracks your style and ensures no clothes go unworn. Smart alerts help you wear 40% more of your closet and save $1,200 yearly.
devpost_first_sections: The fact that we go through life and are willing to spend $2000/year on clothing while only ending up wearing 20% of it. This statistic is commonplace and results in "fashion landfills", which lead to the fashion industry's global emissions jumping by 50% by 2030.

It provides users with a platform to maintain their wardrobes. By giving daily "fit checks", our app can tell the user what kind of clothing items they tend to wear more, giving the user guidelines they can follow next time they go clothes shopping. This app also provides them with an outlet to sell unwanted items, rather than letting them rot in a landfill. This works by emailing a user when it has been some number of days since they last wore a piece of clothing, then giving them the option to automatically list that unwanted item.

glance.what: App guiding people with visual disabilities through their environment.
glance.why: Helps blind users move through spaces independently.

record.what_it_is: A Python assistive app that runs YOLO object detection on a camera feed, announces nearby objects by voice, accepts voice commands to turn vision on or off, and gives turn-by-turn directions to a spoken destination via Google Directions.
record.problem_and_user: People with visual or mobility impairments find everyday travel and routines hard; the app aims to help them get from place to place safely.
record.one_line_pitch: Real-time object detection with spoken feedback and map-based directions to help visually or mobility impaired people get around.
record.problem_statement: People with visual or mobility impairments need help identifying nearby objects and navigating daily routes.
record.devpost_tagline: Seeing the unseen. An app that will help people with visual disabilities to be guided in their environment.
devpost_first_sections: Our team wanted to create a code that would make the world a better world, thus we decided to focus on integrating others. We thought that we could help people with visual disabilities by helping them in their daily routines.

SeeForMe leverages cutting-edge technologies to provide real-time object detection and navigation assistance for individuals with visual or mobility impairments. By using real time object detection and voice feedback, it helps users identify nearby objects like bottles, chairs, stop signs, or cell phones, ensuring they can navigate their environment safely and confidently. The system integrates voice commands for interaction, empowering users to activate or deactivate the vision system, and even request turn-by-turn directions to specific destinations.

glance.what: Two-minute quiz recommending Toyota vehicles matched to your wants and needs.
glance.for_whom: Toyota shoppers unsure what to buy
glance.why: Narrows a huge car catalog to a few vehicles that fit.

record.what_it_is: Quiz-driven Toyota recommender: a two-minute questionnaire on budget, efficiency, seating and tech yields tailored model suggestions with detail pages.
record.problem_and_user: Picking among Toyota's many models is hard; aimed at enthusiasts and first-time buyers.
record.one_line_pitch: Two-minute questionnaire that matches shoppers to a Toyota model based on budget, fuel economy, seating and tech preferences.
record.problem_statement: Choosing among Toyota's wide lineup is overwhelming, especially for first-time buyers.
record.devpost_tagline: DreamDrive is the ideal application to help you find your dream Toyota vehicle. By taking a quick two-minute quiz, we recommend vehicles tailored to all your wants and needs.
devpost_first_sections: Our team was inspired by the excitement of buying a new car and the challenge of finding the perfect vehicle among Toyota’s diverse lineup. We wanted to create a fast, simple, and fun way for anyone, car enthusiasts or first-time buyers alike, to discover a Toyota model that fits their lifestyle, preferences, and budget.

DreamDrive is an interactive application that uses a short two-minute questionnaire to gather a user’s needs and preferences, such as budget, fuel efficiency, seating capacity, tech features, and more. Based on the responses, DreamDrive instantly provides a tailored recommendation of Toyota vehicles that best match the user’s requirements. Whether you’re looking for a family SUV, a sleek sedan, or a reliable hybrid, DreamDrive narrows down the best options so you can feel confident about your choice.

glance.what: Wildfire map predicting fire spread from HPC simulations for anyone to use.
glance.why: Helps decision-makers act fast before wildfires become catastrophic.

record.what_it_is: A solo-built wildfire dashboard where a user types or speaks fire conditions, a Python cellular-automata model projects spread up to 96 hours, and the map flags infrastructure in the path and evacuation routes, with spoken replies.
record.problem_and_user: Incident commanders, first responders and residents in fire-prone areas who need faster, easier-to-use tools to see where a fire is heading and what it will hit.
record.one_line_pitch: Dashboard predicting wildfire spread up to 96 hours with a cellular automata model, flagging affected infrastructure and routes, controllable by voice.
record.target_user: first responders and residents near wildfires
record.problem_statement: People and responders often lack accessible, intuitive tools to understand how a wildfire will spread and what it will reach.
record.devpost_tagline: In a wildfire, a 10-minute delay in decision-making can be the difference between a controlled burn and a massive loss. Cinder Control allows anyone to predict how fires move through HPC calculations.
devpost_first_sections: Cinder Control 🔥🌲

When I was in California when I was little, wildfires were pretty prevalent. I wasn't too aware of what caused them or how they spread, but it feels like every year I've heard another tale of a wildfire demolishing entire cities - and in some cases people aren't even aware they are coming. My hope is that with Cinder Control knowledge and awareness of Wildfires, as well as responding to them, becomes a more intuitive and easy to access process.
